title: The Tracker integrity gate passes when a task record disappears entirely
description:
Found by WCLI-9 while landing it, from a mistake of this session's own making. quest task complete MOVES a record from .quest/tasks/<id>.json to .quest/completed/<id>.json. A commit that staged only the old path recorded a deletion and never added the moved file, so dev and main carried no WCLI-9 record at all -- absent from tasks/ and absent from completed/ -- for two merges. The required Tracker integrity context was green on that commit and on the one after it.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: the job's own steps are "Tracker reads cleanly" (quest task list --json > /dev/null) and "Managed instructions are current" (quest agents --check). Both are satisfied by a tracker that reads cleanly and is missing a record: the first asks whether the tracker parses, not whether the change preserved the records it touched. This is the shape the operating model names -- a check whose clean answer authorises a merge, asked a weaker question than its name promises.

FIX DIRECTION, to be decided rather than assumed: a step that compares the record set across the push (for a pull request, the merge base against the head) and fails when a task id present before is present neither in .quest/tasks/ nor in .quest/completed/ unless the same change records why. Whether a deletion is ever legitimate needs a decision -- quest has no task delete, but archive and migrate exist -- so the honest first step may be to fail on every vanished id and let a real case argue for an exception.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The gap is closed or explicitly accepted in writing: a change that removes a task id from .quest/tasks without that id appearing in .quest/completed fails a required context, and the failure message names the id -- or the task records why record continuity cannot be checked in this repository

The gate is proven both ways on real commits: a deliberate deletion that drops a record without a counterpart fails the new check, and a legitimate quest task complete move passes it, with both runs named in the notes

implementationNotes:
HELD ON DEC-18 (opum-agent OPAG-737), relayed by opum-agent 2026-09-29 after this task was proposed as next work. Do not start it locally: OPAG-737 measured this same Tracker integrity gap passing in 11 of 11 repositories, and the fix — a quest capability (recommended) or a per-repository script — is proposed decision DEC-18, with the operator through opum-doc. A local fix now would get ahead of that decision and may be thrown away. This task's own measurement is kept below as evidence for DEC-18.

EXACT COMMITS AND THE CHECK VERDICT, measured from this repository's history and from GitHub on 2026-09-29. Drop: b2aad11d7cbf79a126e824ca44d1ac540b506ea2, chore(WCLI-9): the task is Done — merged as #58 and promoted to main (#62), committed 2026-09-29T05:13:59Z. At that tree, .quest/tasks/WCLI-9.json is absent and .quest/completed/WCLI-9.json has never been added — git ls-tree at b2aad11 returns nothing for either path, while the tasks/ file is present at b2aad11^. The Tracker integrity context reported SUCCESS on that exact SHA at 2026-09-29T05:14:23Z, with Check and Docs also success: the required gate passed on a tree carrying no WCLI-9 record anywhere. Restore: 19ffee3296a8b523649500090f27dd966943dad8, chore(WCLI-9): restore the completed record the last commit dropped (#63), 2026-09-29T05:17:20Z — the very next commit on dev, since git rev-list --count b2aad11..19ffee3 is 1. Both commits are ancestors of origin/main, so main carried the absent state as well. Absence window on dev: 05:13:59Z to 05:17:20Z.

CLOSED AS SUPERSEDED BY DEC-18 (accepted A), read from opum-ai/opum-agent origin/main 7be97e7, .quest/planning.json: the record-continuity check becomes a quest-cli capability (quest check --continuity --base <ref>, or similar), sequenced as a quest-cli task, then the next lore and quest pair release, then one workflow line per repository, qualified by opum-cli-e2e — explicitly no per-repository script stopgap, which is what this task would have been. This task was already held on DEC-18 by its own note (opum-agent OPAG-737, which measured the same Tracker integrity gap passing in 11 of 11 repositories); the decision resolves the hold by moving the work out of this repository. Nothing is built here, and both acceptance criteria are deliberately left unchecked and are expected to appear as unresolved at completion: the outcome they describe is delivered by quest-cli and then by this repository's later one-line workflow edit, not by a ward-cli change. When the quest capability ships, the ward-cli side is a one-line Tracker integrity workflow edit; it should be filed or covered then rather than reopened here.
